I am not a Rust person, but will this regex catch if the language has a patch version like 1.10.3
https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/cae6a3dfc331918cc422cb3f3c610107c8276d2b/src/modules/elixir.rs#L10
Now that I looked at it again, I do not think that the regex is the problem :)

I wonder if something went wrong with the `0.37.0` release, it doesn't seem to include the `elixir` and `singularity` modules but my local master build does.

```
~/s/r/starship on  master is 📦 v0.37.0 via 🦀 v1.40.0 
❯ starship --version
starship 0.37.0
~/s/r/starship on  master is 📦 v0.37.0 via 🦀 v1.40.0 
❯ starship module --list | grep singularity
~/s/r/starship on  master is 📦 v0.37.0 via 🦀 v1.40.0 
❯ starship module --list | grep elixir
```

```
~/s/r/starship on  master is 📦 v0.37.0 via 🦀 v1.40.0 
❯ target/debug/starship module --list | grep elixir
elixir
~/s/r/starship on  master is 📦 v0.37.0 via 🦀 v1.40.0 
❯ target/debug/starship module --list | grep singularity
singularity
```
Maybe. The `elixir` and `singurality` commits are listed with the commits made after the lastest release: https://github.com/starship/starship/compare/v0.37.0...master
Yep. Looks like they are not released as of version 0.37.0
